speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing agitation and have a yellowish discoloration of your skin and eyes; these symptoms suggest a potential liver issue or severe infection. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any abdominal pain, fever, or changes in your urine or stool color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Viral Hepatitis (likely HIV-associated or sexually transmitted) with possible acute liver failure.
I have noted your history of high-risk sexual behavior and substance use; given your age and symptoms, we need to urgently test for Hepatitis B, C, and HIV, as well as check your liver function levels. Please confirm if you have had any recent contact with needles or shared equipment.
